blocks.text: You can connect your Google Workspace organization to Zscaler 3rd-Party App Governance to gain continuous visibility and governance for third-party apps installed in the Google Workspace environment, including automation of your vetting and governance processes.
A user with Google Admin privileges is required to connect 3rd-Party App Governance to Google Workspace.
Some organizations prefer to use a dedicated service account for new service integrations. We recommend following your standard practice when connecting new services to your business applications.

blocks.heading: Connecting Google Workspace to 3rd-Party App Governance

blocks.text: To connect Google Workspace to 3rd-Party App Governance:

blocks.item: Click Connect in the upper-right corner of the App Dashboard.

blocks.text: See image.

blocks.item: From the drop-down menu, select Google Workspace.

blocks.text: See image.
The Add Integration window appears.

blocks.item: In the Add Integration window, click Add.

blocks.text: See image.
You are redirected to the Add SaaS Application Tenant page in the Zscaler Admin Console.

blocks.item: Enter the tenant details and complete the configuration steps required for adding a new SaaS application tenant. To learn more, see Adding SaaS Application Tenants.

blocks.text: The Add SaaS Application Tenant page closes after successful addition of the new tenant. After a connection is achieved, it might take a while to pull and ingest all relevant application data depending on the size of your tenant. During this time, a message displays indicating that the integration is still being processed. After integration is completed, a success message appears, and the tenant details are updated on the Settings page. You then receive an email from Zscaler when the integration is ready for further review.
You can segregate your Google Workspace integration by organizational units (OUs). This feature is in limited availability. To learn more, contact Zscaler Support.

blocks.heading: Viewing and Managing Google Workspace Integration

blocks.text: You can view the list of added tenants along with information such as integration status, enabled features, first connected time, last synced time, etc. on the Settings page.

blocks.heading: Reconnecting Google Workspace to 3rd-Party App Governance

blocks.text: You might need to reconnect Google Workspace to 3rd-Party App Governance if an error displays (e.g., Grant Expired). To reconnect Google Workspace to 3rd-Party App Governance:

blocks.item: On the Settings page, click the Reconnect icon next to the relevant integration.

blocks.text: A confirmation window appears.
A consent window appears. After consent is granted, the connection is updated.
The Reconnect option is available only for legacy tenants. The existing tenants onboarded via the 3rd-Party App Governance Admin Portal are called legacy tenants.
You can edit a Google Workspace connection to 3rd-Party App Governance. To edit a Google Workspace connection:

blocks.item: On the Settings page, click the Edit icon next to the relevant integration.

blocks.text: You are redirected to the Add SaaS Application Tenant page in the Zscaler Admin Console.

blocks.item: Edit the tenant details as required and click Save.

blocks.text: The connection is updated. The Add SaaS Application Tenant page closes after a successful update.
You can delete a Google Workspace connection to 3rd-Party App Governance. To delete a Google Workspace connection:

blocks.item: On the Settings page, click the Delete icon next to the relevant integration.

blocks.text: A confirmation window appears.
The following step is not required for legacy connections.
You are redirected to the SaaS Application Tenants page in the Zscaler Admin Console, where a confirmation window appears.
The connection is deleted. The SaaS Application Tenants page closes after successful deletion.

blocks.text: The error message This app is blocked appears when connecting 3rd-Party App Governance to your Google Workspace.
See image.
Occasionally, company settings might prevent connecting to third-party apps without explicitly trusting them.
To resolve this issue, add 3rd-Party App Governance to your Google Workspace trusted apps.
To manually trust the integration:

blocks.item: In the Google Admin Console, go to Security > API Controls.

blocks.text: Google Administrative privileges are required for accessing the Google Admin Console.

blocks.item: Under App Access Control, select Manage Third-Party App Access.
Make sure Trusted: can access all Google services is selected, and then click Configure.
Go back to the 3rd-Party App Governance Connect page and connect to Google Workspace again.
